newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Rumours on Suharto health disrupt markets again.
newsitem.headline: Rumours on Suharto health disrupt markets again.

text.p: Rumours that President Suharto would undergo a medical check-up in Germany jolted Indonesia's financial markets again on Friday, even though sources in the presidential palace denied the reports.
"There is no such plan and there's no indication at all the president will have a new medical check-up," one source told Reuters by telephone.
The Indonesian rupiah was driven down to 2,406.5 against the dollar on the strength of the rumours, which dealers said came from Singapore traders, before settling at 2.404.8/05.8 by mid-morning.
On the stock market, trading was slow as most investors remained sidelined following the rumours. At 0400 GMT, the Jakarta composite index was 0.25 percent down at 640.05 points.
Suharto, 75, went to Germany for a medical check-up last year and was declared healthy for the man of his age.

Palace sources said earlier on Friday that Suharto would fulfil his official duties during the day, including meeting the secretary-general of China's state council and participants at a high-ranking meeting of armed forces officials at the Merdeka Palace.
Several Jakarta-based newspapers carried stories and pictures of Suharto on Friday. They denied rumours that he had been ill on Thursday and confirmed he had carried out his normal office duties.
Palace sources said late on Thursday that Suharto was at home and in good health after a normal day's activities, despite renewed rumours on foreign exchange markets that he was ill.
"These rumours are crazy. The president is at home and in good health," one source said.
